subject: Acme Corp - Redwood evaluation & procurement next steps
summary: Post-call recap after discovery call with Acme. Identified economic buyer and procurement path; customer requests 99.9% SLA and a pricing discount. Sales needs internal approvals (discount + SLA + security exception) and legal/security review before sending SOW/quote.
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Carter <e.carter@acmecorp.com>, Tom Hayes <t.hayes@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T16:15:00-07:00
Subject: Acme Corp - Redwood evaluation & procurement next steps

Hi Emily/Tom — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

- Use case: customer-facing knowledge assistant for support docs (low-latency retrieval + safety filters).
- Expected initial throughput: ~30k tokens/day, spiking to ~200k tokens during seasonal peak.
- Decision timeline: procurement review target by 2026-03-20, final decision by ~2026-04-01 per Tom.
- Key stakeholders you flagged: Linda Park (CFO - economic buyer), Sam Wilson (Procurement lead), Emily + Tom (technical + PM).

Action items / next steps:
1) I'll circulate a draft SOW and initial pricing. Attached is our SOW template and the security questionnaire you requested.
2) Emily — can you confirm the procurement contact(s) and whether data residency / SOC 2 evidence are blockers?
3) Tom — you mentioned a 99.9% SLA requirement and potential need for a pricing concession for committed usage. We'll flag this internally and let you know what approvals are needed.

Attachments: Acme-SOW-template-v1.pdf, Acme-Security-Questionnaire-partial.xlsx

Thanks — I'll follow up with an internal ask for approvals if we need to concede on SLA/price.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0183
From: Emily Carter <e.carter@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Hayes <t.hayes@acmecorp.com>, Sam Wilson <s.wilson@acmecorp.com>, Linda Park <l.park@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme Corp - Redwood evaluation & procurement next steps

Thanks Marissa — great recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Confirming stakeholders: Linda (CFO) is the economic buyer; Sam (procurement) will run the T&Cs. I (Emily) will own the technical evaluation and coordinate security questions.
- On security: SOC 2 Type II report and data processing addendum are required. We started filling the questionnaire you sent; see attached partial.
- Timeline: procurement has a checkpoint on 2026-03-20. Ideally we need a finalized commercial term by 2026-03-25 to make the April go/no-go.

Attached: Acme-Security-Questionnaire-partial.xlsx

Can you also confirm whether Redwood can support data residency in AWS us-west-2 for initial deployment?

Thanks,
Emily
Principal Product Manager | Acme Corp
From: Tom Hayes <t.hayes@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Carter <e.carter@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Sam Wilson <s.wilson@acmecorp.com>, Linda Park <l.park@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T14:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme Corp - Redwood evaluation & procurement next steps

Quick note from procurement/PM side:
- Procurement will push back on token-based overages unless we get a committed monthly cap and a predictable unit price.
- Finance/Linda will expect a competitive discount for a 12-month commit. We're hoping for ~15% off list to fit our budget.
- SLA: we need 99.9% uptime in contract. Is that something Redwood can commit to (or an SLA credit door)?

I'll upload procurement redlines later today. If an exception is required for SLA or pricing, please flag internally so we can understand timing.

Thanks,
Tom
Senior PM, Conversational Platforms | Acme Corp
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-04T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Acme Corp - Redwood evaluation & procurement next steps

Folks — forwarding the thread with Acme. Short ask: they are requesting a 15% discount for a 12-month committed usage + a 99.9% SLA (procurement will likely require this in the contract). They also requested SOC 2 evidence and confirmation of data residency in us-west-2.

Why this matters: Acme is a strategic mid-market prospect with clear expansion potential across support+docs. Margin hit at 15% is material but could be justified by ARR potential and referenceability. 

Asks / owners:
- Marcus: are you willing to approve a 15% commercial concession if finance signs off? Please advise on acceptable guardrails (e.g., minimum ARR commit).
- Stephanie: legal — please advise on SLA exceptions and whether we can offer 99.9% with standard credit structure, or if security needs to sign off on any exceptions for data residency / SOC2.
- Dev: can you confirm technical feasibility for initial deployment in us-west-2 and any uplift costs for residency?

Attached earlier in thread: Acme-Procurement-Redlines.docx

Recommend we treat this as an approval path: Commercial -> Finance approval for discount -> Legal/Security sign-off for SLA & residency -> Send SOW + final quote.

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-05T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme Corp - Redwood evaluation & procurement next steps

Marissa — thanks for the summary. A few notes from Legal/Security perspective:

1) SLA: Our standard hosted SLA is 99.95% for paid tiers; we generally don't drop below that publicly. If Acme insists on 99.9% specifically (i.e., lower), that's actually less strict; question is whether procurement wants different credit calculations. We need to review their redlines to ensure no additional operational commitments (e.g., custom monitoring or runbooks).

2) Data residency: We can support deployment in AWS us-west-2 under Redwood Dedicated or Private plans. For Hosted accounts, we need to confirm region availability; Dev, please confirm runbook and estimated lead time.

3) Discount: 15% is within negotiable range but requires finance approval if it affects standard pricing. Marcus — please confirm acceptable approval path and if a margin floor applies. Also include c-level reference potential — if Acme gives a case study, we may be more flexible.

4) Security evidence: we can provide SOC 2 Type II report and a DPA. I'll coordinate with Security to prepare redacted SOC artifacts. Dev, please flag any technical constraints on residency.

I can draft an exception memo for any SLA/term deviations once Marcus confirms commercial.

- Stephanie
Senior Counsel & Head of Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-06T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme Corp - Redwood evaluation & procurement next steps

Marissa — I support moving forward with 15% discount contingent on finance sign-off and a minimum 12-month commit (target ARR >= $60k). If Acme is willing to be a reference and we can get a quick case study, we can be more flexible.

Stephanie — please proceed with drafting any SLA exception memo and prepare SOC/DPA docs to share redacted copies. Dev — coordinate on residency feasibility and estimated timeline/cost uplift.

I'll flag this as a deal to prioritize this week and will engage finance for formal approval.

Marcus
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference
